articles.title: Dozens of Hippos Killed in Anthrax Outbreak
articles.description: Dozens of hippopotamuses have been killed by anthrax in Africa’s oldest national park. The Democratic Republic of the Congo’s 3,000-square-mile, 101-year-old Virunga National Park has seen more than 30 of the enormous mammals die since the outbreak was first reported in September. The park’s conservation chief, Laura Parker, said laboratory analysis had confirmed the deaths. “Park authorities are attributing this to the arrival of significant rainfall, and are cautiously optimistic that there won’t be any further cases, but monitoring protocols continue,” Parker told ABC News. “Anthrax does not exclusively affect hippos, but they are more susceptible due to a combination of their biology and feeding habits,” she added. The World Health Organization reports that anthrax is caused by spore-forming bacteria found in soils around the world. It forms naturally and can remain dormant in soil for extended periods. “Virunga’s response is focused on surveillance, safe carcass management and reducing risks to both wildlife and people,” she said. “Teams have been monitoring the affected area, documenting new mortalities and coordinating the safe handling and disposal of carcasses.” Read it at ABC News Read more at The Daily Beast.

articles.title: Brazil Confirms Fourth Newcastle Disease Outbreak in Santa Catarina
articles.description: Brazil's Ministry of Agriculture has confirmed a fourth case of Newcastle disease (DNC) in a commercial poultry farm within Santa Catarina state. The new outbreak was identified in the municipality of Nova Erechim, an area already designated as a zoosanitary emergency zone. Data from the platform monitoring respiratory and nervous syndromes in birds indicates that the virus was confirmed on Tuesday, December 3, in a turkey production facility. Initial sample collection and the start of the investigation at this site took place on November 31. There are currently four active outbreaks in the country, all localized within the same region, specifically in the municipalities of Nova Itaberaba, Coronel Freitas, and Nova Erechim. The outbreak timeline began on October 18.
